h1: How long does a City Council or ZBA special permit take in Newton, MA?
title: Newton Special Permit Timeline: Public Hearings and Decision Deadlines
description: Review the state statutory hearing and decision deadlines and the Newton City Council's special-permit process.
short_answer: Massachusetts law generally requires a special-permit public hearing within 65 days after the application is filed and a decision within 90 days after the public hearing. The time limits may be extended by written agreement. Newton's City Council is the special-permit granting authority for the City's zoning process, and the full project timeline may be longer because application preparation and review occur before the hearing.

facts.text: Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 40A, Section 9 sets a general 65-day deadline for the special-permit public hearing after filing.
The statute sets a general 90-day period for the decision after the public hearing, subject to a written extension agreement.
Newton's special-permit process involves an application to the City Council and a public hearing before the Land Use Committee.

qa.q: Does the 65-day deadline mean a Newton special permit is always finished within 65 days?
qa.a: No. The 65-day period is the general statutory deadline for holding the public hearing after filing. The decision period follows the hearing, and written extensions may be agreed.
